title: Nested Decisions
objectives: Place one IF inside another IF block (a nested decision)
Do multi-level grade and tier calculations with nested decisions

hook.text: To turn a score into letter grades like AA, BA, BB, and CC, a single IF is not enough. You need to put decisions inside decisions.

concept.heading: An IF inside an IF
concept.body: You can write another IF inside an IF block (or an ELSE block). This is called a nested decision. When the outer condition is FALSE, the inner IF is entered, and it tests its own condition separately.

concept.heading: Checking in tiers
concept.body: A chain of nested IF/ELSE lets you check several thresholds in order: first the highest threshold, otherwise the next one down, otherwise the next one down... This pattern is used a lot in problems like grade calculation and tax brackets.

workedExamples.prompt: Turn a score (0-100) into a letter grade: ≥90 AA, ≥80 BA, otherwise CC.
workedExamples.runnerSource:
grade ← 85
IF grade ≥ 90
  WRITE "AA"
ELSE
  IF grade ≥ 80
    WRITE "BA"
  ELSE
    WRITE "CC"
  END
END

steps.explain: 85 is put into the grade box.
85 ≥ 90 is FALSE, so the ELSE block is entered.
The inner IF is checked: 85 ≥ 80 is TRUE.

exercises.question: When grade ← 95, what does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: The outermost condition (≥90) is already TRUE.

exercises.question: When grade ← 60, what does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: Both conditions are FALSE, so the innermost ELSE block runs.

exercises.question: In a nested IF structure, what happens to the inner IF if the outer condition is TRUE?
options: It is never checked, it is skipped
It is automatically treated as TRUE

feedback.correct: Correct. When the outer condition is TRUE, the inner IF inside the ELSE is never entered.
feedback.incorrect: If the outer condition is TRUE, the inner IF inside the ELSE block is never run.

exercises.question: Put the steps of an algorithm that calculates a three-tier shipping fee (≥10 kg expensive, ≥5 kg medium, otherwise cheap) in the correct order.
When grade ← 75, what does this code write to the screen?
Complete the sentence.

summary: You can write another IF inside an IF (or ELSE) block. This is called a nested decision.
If the outer condition is TRUE, the inner IF is never run.
A chain of nested IF/ELSE is used for multi-tier threshold checks (grades, tax brackets, and so on).
